papers.title: Sleep Homeostasis Has Circaseptan and Circatrigintan Cycles Over Year-Long Timescales.
papers.summary: Using continuous subscalp EEG in 20 healthy adults over 12–15 months, this study characterized long-term sleep homeostatic dynamics via the nightly rate of decline in slow-wave activity (0.5–4 Hz). SWA slope was predominantly negative and stable across sex and age, and continuous wavelet transform analysis revealed significant circaseptan (~7-day) and circatrigintan (~28-day) rhythmicity in most subjects.

papers.title: Tau-driven hyperexcitability of locus coeruleus noradrenergic neurons underlies sleep fragmentation and cognitive decline in mice.
papers.summary: Using P301S mice and cell-type-specific tau overexpression, the authors show that pathological tau selectively increases intrinsic excitability of locus coeruleus noradrenergic (LCDBH) neurons, producing sleep fragmentation, reduced NREM sleep and slow-wave activity, and recognition memory deficits. Optogenetic suppression of LCDBH-tau neuronal activity reversed sleep disturbances and rescued cognitive dysfunction.

papers.title: DPYD links glial lipids and myelination to sleep duration
papers.summary: Across mouse, zebrafish, Drosophila, and human genetic data, this study shows that DPYD and its orthologs act in glia to promote sleep through regulation of brain lipids, with loss reducing myelination and sleep independently of uracil catabolism. Manipulating myelination in zebrafish was sufficient to perturb sleep duration, and a human GWAS sleep variant was localized to a conserved oligodendrocyte-specific cis-regulatory element contacting the DPYD promoter.

papers.title: Standard touchscreen test procedures shift circadian rhythms in mice: a modified protocol to minimize circadian confounds
papers.summary: After observing circadian phase shifting in mice tested with standard touchscreen procedures during the early dark period, this study attributed the shift to light emitted by the touchscreen chambers, which induced a ~3.5 h phase delay after 7 consecutive training days. Testing 10 modified lighting conditions, the authors provide protocol recommendations that minimize circadian confounds without impairing visual discrimination or TUNL task performance.

papers.title: Closed-loop acoustic stimulation promotes local slow oscillation train initiation and persistence in elderly adults
papers.summary: Investigated whether closed-loop acoustic stimulation (CLAS) alters slow oscillation (SO) temporal organization in elderly adults by comparing stimulated (n=16) and sham (n=11) nights. Locally, CLAS reduced isolated SOs and increased consecutive SOs, train-initiation probability, and mean train length, with weaker but directionally consistent global overnight effects.

papers.title: Thalamic stereo-EEG detects sleep stages N2 and N3 with discrimination approaching scalp EEG
papers.summary: Analyzed 477 h of simultaneous stereo-EEG and scalp EEG from six adults to test whether thalamic channels identify sleep stages N2+N3. Thalamic channels achieved AUCs of 0.94 (RF+HMM) and 0.93 (SleepSEEG) and outperformed mesial temporal and temporal neocortical channels in all six participants.

papers.title: AIM-STAGE: a self-supervised framework via adaptive interval-aware multi-kernel calibration and spectro-temporal exploration for few-shot EEG staging.
papers.summary: Proposes AIM-STAGE, a self-supervised framework combining STFT spectro-temporal features, CNN-Transformer encoding, and adaptive interval-aware multi-kernel calibration for few-shot EEG sleep staging. It outperformed six baselines across four datasets from 1% to 15% labels, raising accuracy from 88.67% to 92.04% on SLEEP-2013, with N1 remaining the hardest stage.

papers.title: Circadian multimodal physiological, ocular and behavioural data from a 40-hour forced-desynchrony protocol
papers.summary: This paper presents a multimodal dataset from 12 healthy adults who completed a 40-hour ultra-short forced-desynchrony protocol (2 h 30 min wake in dim light, 1 h 15 min sleep in darkness, 3 h 45 min ultradian cycle) to decouple circadian and homeostatic influences. Repeated wake-interval assessments included chromatic temporal contrast sensitivity, pupillometry, optical coherence tomography, intraocular pressure, psychomotor vigilance, salivary hormones, actigraphy, ECG, temperature, blood pressure, and interstitial glucose.

papers.title: Anti-correlation time-frequency synergy and dual-granularity fusion for sleep stage classification.
papers.summary: Designs a single-channel EEG sleep staging network using anti-correlated multi-branch frequency features, dual-granularity residual attention fusion, causal transition-aware learning, and focal loss. It reached overall accuracies of 87.0%, 83.4%, and 84.5% on SleepEDF-20, SleepEDF-78, and SHHS, with N1 accuracies of 57.5%, 52.5%, and 49.3%.

papers.title: A hypothalamo-septo-hippocampal circuit for REM sleep-dependent consolidation of social memory
papers.summary: Identified a lateral supramammillary nucleus (SuM)-medial septum (MS) projection selectively active during REM sleep; REM-specific optogenetic silencing impaired consolidation of social and contextual fear memories, while silencing the downstream MS-CA2 pathway selectively disrupted social memory. Establishes a hypothalamo-septo-hippocampal (lateral SuM-MS-CA2) circuit dedicated to REM sleep-dependent social memory consolidation.

papers.title: Slow power-envelope associations among brain, heart, and gut signals during sleep: an exploratory multivariate transfer entropy study.
papers.summary: Applied multivariate transfer entropy to overnight occipital EEG, ECG, and bowel sound signals from 24 healthy subjects to quantify directed slow power-envelope associations among brain, heart, and gut across sleep stages. Information flow from heart to brain, brain to gut, and heart to gut consistently exceeded reverse directions, with stage-dependent inter-system patterns such as suppressed heart-to-gut and brain-to-gut flow in deep sleep.

papers.title: Enhancing deep sleep with auditory stimulation to boost cognitive training responsiveness in people with Parkinson's disease and mild cognitive impairment: Rationale and design of the double-blind randomized controlled trial PD-CogT-Sleep
papers.summary: Describes the rationale and design of PD-CogT-Sleep, a double-blind randomized sham-controlled trial combining remotely delivered digital cognitive training with phase-targeted auditory stimulation (PTAS) to enhance deep sleep in people with Parkinson's disease and mild cognitive impairment. Primary outcome is executive function, with cognitive, patient-reported, blood biomarker, and high-density sleep EEG outcomes assessed at baseline, five weeks, and 3-month follow-up in 50 planned participants.

papers.title: Psychomotor vigilance is multidimensional: evidence from index network analysis, parameter review, and neuroimaging.
papers.summary: Reviews PVT stimulus modality, task duration, interstimulus interval, and index calculation, and reports an exploratory network analysis of 15 PVT indices in 678 participants supporting a three-group Stable/Overall/Control framework. Integrates EEG and fMRI findings linking vigilance to waking oscillations, network stability, prior sleep physiology, and functional connectivity.

papers.title: Dynamics of Sleep Architecture and Nocturnal Oxygen Saturation During Acclimatization at Intermediate Altitude: A Longitudinal Observational Study in Elite Athletes.
papers.summary: In 17 elite mogul-ski athletes undergoing a 2-week camp at 2100 m, wearable EEG-oximetry showed total sleep time was unchanged but %N3 declined and %REM rose logarithmically across the first week, while SpO2 was lower and overnight heart rate higher than in normoxia, with SpO2 recovery occurring fastest in N1 and REM and slowest in N2/N3. The authors conclude that acclimatization dynamics are sleep-stage-specific and that the first two nights capture the most rapid adjustments.

papers.title: Photoentrainment as Bayesian Inference: How the central circadian clock may weight and integrate the intensity and wavelength of natural light to estimate astronomical time
papers.summary: Presents a Bayesian model in which the central circadian clock predicts distributions of light intensity and spectral composition given time of day and adjusts phase according to prediction error weighted by relative reliability. Using natural light data from 59 human observers and 100 days of spectral measurements, shows how light variability across the day can generate the canonical phase response curve shape.

papers.title: Poor Test-Retest Stability of Nocturnal REM Sleep Onset Markers in Narcolepsy Type 1.
papers.summary: In 227 untreated children and adults with narcolepsy type 1 who underwent two overnight polysomnograms, nocturnal sleep-onset REM periods (nSOREMPs) showed poor test-retest agreement (κ=0.26), present on both nights in only 41.8%, and nocturnal direct REM transitions were similarly unstable; persistence was associated with younger age, shorter MSLT sleep latency, and lower CSF hypocretin-1, suggesting variable REM dysregulation rather than a stable trait.

papers.title: Transient Alerting Effects of Karolinska Sleepiness Scale Ratings on Physiological and Driving Performance Indicators.
papers.summary: Pooled data from five driving simulator studies (83 participants) to test whether Karolinska Sleepiness Scale (KSS) ratings produce transient alerting effects. Immediately after rating, blink duration and lateral position variability decreased, blink closing velocity and heart rate increased, and parietal alpha power decreased, with transient durations ranging from 40 s to beyond 120 s depending on the indicator.

papers.title: Automated Sleep Staging: Are Algorithms Ready for the Clinic?
papers.summary: This review examines AI-based automated sleep staging programs as a means to reduce scoring time and improve standardization, while emphasizing that clinical implementation requires models trained on heterogeneous data covering both common and infrequent sleep disorders and that clinicians recognize these limitations before integration into workflows.

papers.title: How Circadian Rhythms Shape Emotional Reactivity and Regulation: A Narrative Review.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence that circadian misalignment, including evening chronotype, social jet lag, and shift work, is associated with greater negative affect, impaired emotion regulation, and increased psychiatric symptoms. It highlights methodological inconsistencies and recommends combining subjective reports with physiological markers, longitudinal designs, and circadian-informed interventions.

papers.title: Multimodal Artificial Intelligence for Sleep: Integrating Multichannel Signals for Comprehensive Assessment.
papers.summary: This review examines five frontiers of multimodal AI in sleep medicine: foundation models pre-trained on diverse biosignal datasets, automated sleep staging matching expert reliability, AI-driven respiratory analysis moving beyond the Apnea-Hypopnea Index toward endotype-level characterization, and AI-derived sleep biomarkers such as EEG microstructure and brain age.

papers.title: Distinct Systemic Metabolic Remodeling and Neurobehavioral Deterioration in Chemotherapy-Treated Lung Cancer Models.
papers.journal: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
papers.summary: Comparing chemotherapy-treated subcutaneous and orthotopic Lewis lung carcinoma mouse models, the authors found divergent survival and neurobehavioral trajectories, with orthotopic tumors showing greater systemic deterioration and broader plasma metabolic remodeling (ketone body, glutathione, one-carbon, redox pathways). Both models showed peripheral oxidative stress and brain changes involving Claudin-5, glial activation, and synaptic markers.

papers.title: A single day of natural daylight exposure and physical activity does not conclusively change circadian phase: A Bayesian crossover experiment
papers.summary: In a Bayesian crossover experiment with 41 healthy adults, a single 8-h natural daylight exposure with or without ~4 h hiking did not conclusively shift circadian phase, with estimated DLMO changes of -4.22 min per SD increase in illuminance and -6.48 min per SD increase in heart rate reserve. Exploratory sleepiness, mood, wellbeing, exertion, and vigilance outcomes were largely inconclusive or negligible.

papers.title: Cannabidiol and fronto-parietal EEG connectivity in autistic children.
papers.summary: In a double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial, resting-state EEG from autistic children (n=18 analyzed) showed increased beta-band right fronto-parietal (F4-P8) functional connectivity after 12 weeks of oral cannabidiol versus placebo, with no significant placebo-period changes. The authors present this as preliminary evidence requiring replication in larger samples.

papers.title: Sleep and Neurodegeneration: Artificial Intelligence Applications in Early Detection and Personalized Care.
papers.summary: This review examines evidence linking sleep disturbances, glymphatic clearance of misfolded proteins, and neurodegeneration, and assesses AI applications such as automated sleep staging, wearable monitoring, and digital therapeutics for early detection and personalized sleep health promotion.

papers.title: Protocol for cell-type-specific circadian bioluminescence recording from mouse gut muscularis externa explants.
papers.summary: Describes a protocol for generating intestinal cell-type-specific PER2::CBG-LUC reporter mice, preparing longitudinal muscle-myenteric plexus explants, and performing long-term bioluminescence recording with a photomultiplier-based photon counting system. The protocol includes analysis of circadian phase and rhythmicity and verification that ex vivo rhythms reflect the endogenous in vivo circadian phase.

papers.title: Tick tock: how the body's circadian clock keeps cardiometabolic rhythm in check.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes mechanistic roles of core circadian clock genes and central and peripheral clocks in cardiometabolic health, describing how chronodisruption from shift work, irregular sleep, artificial light at night, and erratic eating promotes hormonal dysregulation, inflammation, and metabolic impairment. It discusses pharmacological clock modulation and personalized chronotherapy as emerging strategies.

papers.title: Supporting the driver's perception cognition action loop using an embodied intelligent cockpit framework for explainable fatigue intervention.
papers.summary: Evaluated an embodied intelligent cockpit framework combining multimodal fatigue detection (EEG, eye tracking, vehicle dynamics), SHAP-based feature attribution, and LLM-generated state-specific auditory feedback in 40 drivers during simulated conditional automated driving. Explanatory speech yielded a 0.192-s shorter mean braking reaction time and 0.085-m lower SDLP versus generic speech; retrospective leave-one-subject-out AUC was 0.85.

papers.title: Augmented cardiac growth hormone signaling in circadian-disrupted cardiomyopathy.
papers.summary: This minireview proposes that the cardiac growth hormone axis mediates circadian-disruption-induced cardiomyopathy, suggesting the cardiomyocyte molecular clock, plausibly via REV-ERBα, restricts GH responsiveness and that mistimed GH signaling promotes hypertrophy, fibrosis, and metabolic inflexibility. It cites cardiomyocyte-specific Bmal1-deficient mice showing increased GH-induced STAT5 phosphorylation, Igf1 expression, and remodeling partially attenuated by reduced GH receptor dosage.

papers.title: Associations between objective sleep outcomes and performance on neurocognitive tests used to guide sport-related concussion diagnosis and management: a pilot study.
papers.summary: In a pilot study of 20 athletes whose sleep was tracked by dry-EEG for 4-5 nights before baseline testing, REM sleep percentage was strongly correlated with SCAT5 Concentration score (ρ=0.71) and predicted it in exploratory regression (β=0.49), suggesting pre-test REM sleep loss may confound SCAT concentration testing.

papers.title: BMAL1-Sleep interactions modulate quality of life in allergic rhinitis patients with circadian dysregulation.
papers.summary: Compared 100 allergic rhinitis patients with 33 healthy controls on chronotype, sleep quality, quality of life, and peripheral leukocyte circadian CLOCK gene expression. Patients showed poorer sleep, more evening chronotypes, and dysregulated CLOCK/PER1/BMAL1/CRY1 expression, with BMAL1 expression positively correlated with RQLQ scores and interacting with sleep duration on activity limitations and sleep efficiency on nasal symptoms.

papers.title: Environmental enrichment is associated with changes in the gut microbiome and resistome of captive pythons.
papers.summary: Using shotgun metagenomic sequencing of Burmese and reticulated pythons before and after environmental enrichment, the authors report host-dependent shifts in gut microbiome composition, with increased alpha-diversity and carbohydrate metabolism potential in Burmese pythons. Pseudomonadota contributed most antibiotic resistance genes, indicating enrichment-associated changes in the gut resistome.

papers.title: Intraoperative electroencephalography burst suppression during endoscopic third ventriculostomy: Case report and implications for neuromonitoring.
papers.summary: Case report of a 28-year-old woman undergoing endoscopic third ventriculostomy for obstructive hydrocephalus in whom endoscope insertion and ventricular irrigation provoked two episodes of tachycardic hypertensive crisis coinciding with bilateral EEG burst suppression; hemodynamics normalized within 15 min but EEG recovery took 55 min. The authors suggest processed intraoperative EEG may serve as an early sign of acute cerebral disturbance, while noting its added value remains unproven.

papers.title: Chronotherapy and Circadian Medicine: Personalizing Treatment Timing with Artificial Intelligence.
papers.summary: This review describes how AI algorithms applied to wearable sensors, blood transcriptomes, and multimodal physiologic data can estimate individual circadian phase to personalize treatment timing (light therapy, chemotherapy, antiseizure and antihypertensive drugs), while discussing barriers in data standardization, regulation, and clinical integration and critically reviewing controversial trials such as Hygia.

papers.title: Tian Wang Bu Xin Dan Attenuates Neuronal Injury in LPS-Treated HT22 Cells and PCPA-Induced Insomnia-Model Rats.
papers.summary: A cinnabar-free modified Tian Wang Bu Xin Dan extract was profiled by LC-MS and network analysis, then tested in LPS-treated HT22 cells and PCPA-induced insomnia rats, where it shifted PI3K/AKT, autophagy (Beclin 1, LC3-II/LC3-I, p62), inflammation, and apoptosis markers toward control levels and improved sleep responses, anxiety-like behavior, spatial learning, and hippocampal CA1 injury.

papers.title: Multiscale Neurodynamic Alterations in Major Depressive Disorder Revealed by Lempel-Ziv Complexity of Multi-Paradigm Resting-State EEG.
papers.summary: Using multiscale Lempel-Ziv complexity on resting-state EEG across eyes-open and eyes-closed paradigms, the study found impaired complexity transitions from low to high frequencies and disrupted delta-centered cross-scale integration in MDD patients versus controls, with classification models reaching up to 85.71% accuracy.

papers.title: Resting-State EEG Graph Analysis Reveals Enhanced Alpha-Band Integration in High-IQ Individuals: The MENSA-Connect Project.
papers.summary: Resting-state 64-channel EEG with Lagged Linear Coherence and graph-theory analysis in 29 MENSA members versus 20 controls showed lower alpha-band characteristic path length (greater global integration) and higher beta-band clustering coefficient with higher path length (greater local specialization) in high-IQ individuals, with no small-worldness differences.

papers.title: In-person UCLA-PEERS® program for adolescents with autism spectrum disorder in Italy: study protocol for a pilot and feasibility randomized controlled trial with pragmatic features and exploratory EEG markers of treatment response.
papers.summary: Protocol for a two-arm pilot and feasibility randomized controlled trial comparing in-person UCLA PEERS® with treatment as usual in 36 Italian adolescents with autism spectrum disorder Level 1, with primary focus on feasibility (recruitment, retention, attendance, fidelity) and exploratory clinical outcomes including social functioning. Baseline EEG N400 congruency effect during a gesture-word integration task will be explored as a marker of treatment response.

papers.title: Immunometabolic reprogramming: a working framework for disease development, endotype differentiation, and therapeutic considerations in pediatric asthma.
papers.summary: This review integrates evidence on immunometabolic reprogramming in pediatric asthma and proposes a "Metabolic Latching Model" in which early-life insults establish persistent inflammatory memory through metabolism-epigenetic coupling. It prioritizes testable hypotheses on monocyte glycolytic baseline predicting wheeze-to-asthma transition, metabolic intervention in obese asthma, and the HDAC2-GSH/butyrate axis in steroid sensitivity.

papers.title: Tirzepatide for the treatment of obstructive sleep apnea: from apnea-hypopnea index reduction to cardiometabolic risk mitigation-a narrative review.
papers.summary: This narrative review evaluates tirzepatide, the first FDA-approved pharmacotherapy for moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity, anchoring evidence in the SURMOUNT-OSA trial program. In SURMOUNT-OSA, tirzepatide produced randomized, placebo-controlled reductions in apnea-hypopnea index, sleep apnea-specific hypoxic burden, body weight, and systemic inflammation, though cardiovascular, renal, and mortality signals derive only from nonrandomized observational cohorts and remain exploratory.

papers.title: Sphenoidal Meningioma with Focal Seizures Masquerading as Immune Reconstitution Inflammatory Syndrome in HIV Patient.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 47-year-old woman with HIV who developed recurrent focal-onset seizures evolving to bilateral tonic-clonic seizures about four weeks after starting antiretroviral therapy, initially suggesting immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome, but imaging revealed a 3.0 × 4.3 cm left sphenoid wing meningioma. Gross total surgical resection achieved seizure freedom at 12 months, highlighting the need for a broad differential diagnosis and integration of clinical, electrophysiological, infectious, and imaging data in adults with HIV.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
